cards.title: One warm-remount read cache for the Chores depth's daemon reads
shared_surfaces: docs/adr/0144-the-chores-depth-keeps-its-daemon-reads-warm-across-a-move.md (ADR number to be taken at build time)
acceptance: reads.ts: two `read(key, fetch)` calls for the same key (same client object, same route key) while the first is in flight -> fetch called once, both callers get the one answer (in-flight dedup)

reads.ts: an entry answered for client A is never served to client B with the same route key -> B starts cold (`looking`), fetch called for B (client identity is part of the key, as useCases' `answer.client` check does today)

topic: warm paint, then the revalidation rejects with ApiError(0,'offline') -> the cached case stays drawn and one line says it could not be refreshed because the daemon is not running (failure keeps stale truth visible); the cold-failure wording of casesLine is unchanged
topic: revalidation answers a newer approval (approved_rev 3) -> the page shows `draft 3` replacing `draft 2` with no intermediate `Looking` state
memory: forgetChores() clears the read cache -> the next mount starts cold and says `Looking for a case you saved...` (test isolation stays as today)
topic: first ever visit with deps -> `Looking for a case you saved...` while the answer is on its way, exactly as the existing test pins

cards.body:
## Summary
The Chores depth reads three things from the daemon (a chore's saved cases, each case's runs, each case's cadence) and keeps every answer in the component that asked. The stage remounts the view on every move, so each return from the studio or the replay repaints `Your case` and `Your runs` cold, from `Looking...`, and asks again. One module-scoped read cache (`reads.ts`) keyed by (client, route key), stale-while-revalidate with in-flight dedup, replaces both hand-rolled hooks and makes the page paint warm on return.

## Description
`memory.ts` already exists because a move remounts: the catalogue filters, the intro and the scroll offsets live in module scope. The daemon reads were never given the same treatment. `useCases` (topic.tsx:56) and `useRuns` (runs.tsx:25) are two copies of one pattern: a `useState` answer tagged with what it answered and which client, returning `looking` until the promise settles. On a remount that is always `looking`. The visible cost is the bottom of the topic page: the cases list collapses to one status line and each case's runs to another, while `useLayoutEffect` restores a scroll offset measured on the full page. In a real webview the offset is clamped to the short page and the person lands above where they left, then the content grows under them. jsdom does not clamp, which is why wired.test.tsx:201 passes.

The move is registry `client-fetch-cache`, technique `warm-remount-caches` (a module-scoped last result that a remount reads synchronously and revalidates behind), with `in-flight-dedup` and `cache-key-discipline` (client identity in the key, as the current hooks already check). Following `swr-design`, a failed revalidation keeps the cached value drawn and says it could not be refreshed. The state the hook returns tells `looking` (nothing yet), `found` (fresh) and `found, refreshing` / `found, refresh failed` apart, so the page never shows a stale answer as fresh.

Out of scope: `due.tsx` (owned by desktop-tasks-and-due) keeps its own load. Its owner can move it onto `reads.ts` in one later commit, and the ADR names that.

## Flow
- reads.ts: `readKey(client, route)`, `useRead(key, fetch)` -> `{kind:'looking'} | {kind:'found', value, refreshing, refreshFailed?} | {kind:'failed', ...}`, a Map bounded by the depth's working set (cases per chore, runs per case; at most 20 cases by the daemon's own cut), `forgetReads()` for tests
- topic.tsx: `useCases` becomes a thin adapter over `useRead`; `casesLine` keeps its words, plus one line for a failed refresh over a warm value
- runs.tsx: `useRuns` likewise; `runsLine` unchanged
- memory.ts: `forgetChores()` also forgets reads
- ADR: the depth's daemon reads outlive the move, revalidate on every warm paint, and keep stale truth visible on a failed refresh

## Expected impact
Coming back from the studio or the replay paints `Your case` and `Your runs` as they were, with no layout jump under the restored scroll. The N+1 read burst on every return becomes a background revalidation per key, deduplicated. The depth stops carrying two copies of a keyed fetch, and the next read (catalogue `Yours`, Due) has one place to go.

## Evaluation
Claim: the topic page paints the daemon's last answers synchronously after a move, revalidates once per key, and keeps a stale answer visible when the refresh fails.
Before: 4 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the guard cases 4, 6, 7 and the cold-visit wording; cases 0-3 and 5 fail: no dedup, no warm paint)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (vitest, jsdom, FakeClient as in topic.test.tsx)
Result: better
Gate: none

Registry: client-fetch-cache golden path (revision 15), techniques warm-remount-caches, swr-design, in-flight-dedup, cache-key-discipline.

cards.body:
## Summary
The Chores root is the shipped library: about a hundred playbooks ordered by the author's scores. A person who has adopted three of them, one of which came due yesterday, sees the same page as a first-time visitor. Their own cases, what is due and what is running sit two levels down, on each chore's topic page, and the person has to remember which chores they were. Put a `Your chores` band at the top of the catalogue, listing every saved case joined to its chore, open reviews first, each one press from its case or its page. Add a `Yours` toggle that narrows the ledger to chores that have a case.

## Description
The daemon already answers the data: `GET /adopt/cases` with no playbook lists every case (routes.py:218, cases.py:317), and each case's open review is `GET /adopt/cases/<proj>/review` on the chores client the depth already holds. Today the catalogue is never handed those clients (view.tsx:98). A pure `yours.ts` joins cases to the shipped set and orders them: an open review first (`Due <day>`, `and N missed`), then latest approval. It names a case whose chore this build does not ship instead of dropping it, and passes the daemon's `(showing N of M)` through. The catalogue draws the band only when it has deps, so the preview, the perf gate's first fixture and a window with no daemon render exactly as today. Each state is said in words (looking, none saved, offline, refused), following the topic page's `casesLine` vocabulary.

The due notice in the dock is offered once and stamped seen (due-poll.ts). After that, nothing on the Chores root says the chore is still waiting. The band is the place a person can see what is waiting for them and act on it. Today the surface only reports.

If card A (warm-remount reads) lands first, the band reads through `reads.ts` and the rise from a topic paints warm. Without it, the band uses the same keyed load as useCases, so the two cards do not depend on each other.

## Flow
- view.tsx: pass `adopt` and `go` to Catalogue
- yours.ts (pure): `yoursOf(model, cases, reviews)` -> rows, an unknown-chore count, a footer; `yoursLine(state)` for the no-row states; `hasCase(model, cases)` for the toggle
- catalogue.tsx: the band above the tabs (a list of rows: chore name as a link to its page, case title, due or last-approved line, `Open your case`); a `Yours` toggle in the job bar
- memory.ts: `CatalogueState.yours: boolean`
- fixtures.ts / index.tsx: a `ledger-yours` fixture with a scripted client (two cases, one open review), so the preview and the capture can show the band
- chores.css: the band, inside the existing pa- family, tokens only

## Expected impact
A returning person sees their own chores first, and sees which one is waiting, on the screen they land on. Opening the case they mean takes one press instead of a hunt through the ledger plus two levels of navigation. The only answer to "what is due" stops being a notice that disappears once shown.

## Evaluation
Claim: the catalogue lists every saved case joined to its chore, with open reviews first, opens each in one press, narrows the ledger to the person's chores, and is unchanged without a daemon.
Before: 1 of 8 acceptance cases pass (case 7, the no-deps guard)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (vitest: pure yours.ts tests plus jsdom catalogue tests with a FakeClient as in topic.test.tsx)
Result: better
Gate: none
